newsitem.title: GERMANY: Historic Berlin square could be named after Brandt.
newsitem.headline: Historic Berlin square could be named after Brandt.

text.p: Berlin's Social Democrats (SPD) proposed on Wednesday that one of the German capital's most historic squares should be named after Willy Brandt, the SPD chancellor who was an architect of East-West detente.
Berlin's SPD chairman Detlef Dzembritzki said that, four years after Brandt's death, it was time to honour Brandt by naming the square in front of the Reichstag parliament building after him.

The grassy area currently carries the name Platz der Republik (Republic Square), and was the place where an enormous German flag was hoisted on October 3, 1990 to mark the unification of East and West Germany.
SPD parliamentary deputy Philipp Scheidemann proclaimed the first German republic on the same square in 1918.
During the 1948-49 Soviet blockade of West Berlin, city mayor Ernst Reuter appealed for help to the Western world from the same spot with the words "Peoples of the world, look on this city".
Brandt, also a former Berlin mayor, was the architect of the "Ostpolitik" which ushered in a thaw in Cold War superpower relations in the 1970s, eventually paving the way for unification.

The area around the Reichstag is currently subject to major building work to prepare for parliament and the government to move from Bonn in 1999, and the final shape of the square has not yet been decided on.
